product: commentary — no product (a long essay on influencer marketing vs UGC vs founder-led content)
hook: "'Is influencer marketing dead?'" — question hook, asked from a medieval castle hike.
body: A founder shifted spend to performance-based UGC (budget + hooks/script/CTA briefed, parceled to random creators, pay on performance) after micro-influencers overcharged for flops; but his best-performing UGC clip was "a comedy sketch with no real CTA, no brand lift" — "funding someone else's sketch comedy career"; the pitch: founders should make their own content ("be your own influencer") since nobody knows the business better.
cta: none (essay closer: "go for a walk and touch grass").
idea: The comedy-sketch trap: a funny sketch can be the best-performing clip while delivering zero brand lift — entertainment without a DR spine funds the creator's career, not the brand's growth.
sequencing: The question (is influencer marketing dead?)
The founder's shift (performance UGC)
The reveal (best clip = comedy sketch, no CTA, no lift)
The indictment (funding a sketch career)
The solution (founder-led content)
The closer (be your own influencer)
formatting: Long text post + photo; essay style.
why_it_works: "Funding someone else's sketch comedy career" is a devastating, memorable line — it names the exact failure mode of comedy ads (laughs without lift) in a way that sticks.
what_to_steal: The DR-spine rule for LC's comedy sketches: every sketch must carry the mechanism + CTA (waterproof demo, shop link) — laughs are the vehicle, never the destination.

product: commentary — no product (a golfer's reaction to a brand's failed funny ad; brand mentioned: Callaway)
hook: "The sad part is that this brand thought this was going to be a funny ad." — schadenfreude opener.
body: A golfer reacts to Callaway's attempt at a funny ad ("I have pulled the calaway woods from my bag") — the joke being he'd rather pull the clubs than watch the ad; tagged #calawaygolf #goodgood.
idea: Failed comedy ads get publicly roasted by their own audience — the post is a specimen of what happens when the sketch isn't actually funny.
sequencing: The verdict (brand thought it'd be funny)
The reaction (pulled the woods from the bag)
The tags
The travel proof (11,787 views — the roast traveled)
formatting: Short text post; 11,787 views — the roast traveled.
why_it_works: As a cautionary specimen: an unfunny "funny ad" doesn't just flop, it becomes content FOR the audience's jokes — the brand pays to be the punchline.
what_to_steal: The pre-flight bar for LC comedy: if the sketch isn't funny to a cold viewer in 3 seconds, it's a brand-damage ad, not a comedy ad — kill it before spend.

product: QuietSeal (a fake spec brand invented for this demo — an anti-snoring product; not a real product)
hook: "What if an anti-snoring ad felt more like a ridiculous comedy sketch than an ad? So I made one." — concept-first maker framing.
body: A self-made spec ad: claymation characters, absurd escalation, deadpan voiceover, for a fake anti-snoring brand called QuietSeal; the stated goal: "make you watch the story before you realize you're watching a product ad."
cta: none visible (spec demo; link to the video).
idea: Story-first camouflage — absurd escalation + deadpan VO in claymation earns the watch, and the product reveal lands only after the viewer is invested in the story.
sequencing: The what-if (comedy sketch instead of ad)
The build (claymation, absurd escalation, deadpan VO, fake brand)
The goal (story before product realization)
The spec-ad status (fake brand demo — structure, not proof of conversion)
why_it_works: "Watch the story before you realize you're watching a product ad" is the comedy-DR thesis in one line — narrative investment precedes sales resistance.
what_to_steal: The story-first structure for LC: a ridiculous sketch (e.g., a woman showering/swimming/running in full jewelry while everyone else removes theirs) where the waterproof reveal lands as the punchline.
